intent: "Done with this thread" — worked, not ignored

input_schema.title: conversation.close input
input_schema.description: One thread, set aside as worked. The thread names itself; the campaign is the work item's, carried for context.

external_id.description: The provider's identifier for the thread, as `conversation.list` returned it.

idempotency_key.description: The work item's own identifier, stable across every attempt.

external_ids.description: Only this plugin's own pins reach it, so another provider's identifier is never visible here.

items.description: One outcome for the one thread.

status.description: The thread is closed now, whether or not it was before: the provider does not say.

failure_codes.when: The provider holds no thread under this identifier, or not one this account may see. Nothing was changed.
The provider account's plan or role does not include this capability, so no call by this account can perform it.
The vendor tool refused the call or never started, so nothing the operation asks for was ever attempted. Repeating it runs the same broken call.
The plugin's own credential does not let it change this account's threads.
The provider refused the call for now and it may be attempted again.
The provider could not be reached, or answered with a failure on its own side, before anything was written.
The provider was called and no answer arrived, so the thread may already be closed. Closing a closed thread changes nothing, so the next attempt simply asks again.

conformance: The thread is closed whatever its state was, and a second performance leaves it as the first did, which is what makes a repeat after a lost answer safe.
Closing a thread records no business outcome and stops no outreach: nothing about the person, their participation or the suppression register changes.
